learning_path:
**6-Month Data Science Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Month 1 | COU4368 | Introduction to Data Science Specialization | Coursera | Foundational building block, covers data science basics |
| Month 2 | COU5253 | SQL for Data Science | Coursera | Builds on previous course, focuses on SQL skills |
| Month 3 | COU5245 | Data Science Fundamentals with Python and SQL Specialization | Coursera | Introduces Python programming and data science concepts |
| Month 4 | COU5745 | Data Science Foundations Specialization | Coursera | Covers data acquisition, project management, and machine learning |
| Month 5 | COU4377 | What is Data Science? | Coursera | Provides a broad understanding of data science and its applications |
| Month 6 | COU5907 | Data Science at Scale - Capstone Project | Coursera | Applies learned skills to a real-world project, emphasizing data wrangling, statistics, and data analysis |

This learning path starts with a foundational course in data science (COU4368), followed by a course that focuses on SQL skills (COU5253). The next course (COU5245) introduces Python programming and data science concepts, building on the previous two courses. The fourth month's course (COU5745) covers data acquisition, project management, and machine learning, further expanding the learner's skills. The fifth month's course (COU4377) provides a broad understanding of data science and its applications. Finally, the sixth month's course (COU5907) applies learned skills to a real-world project, emphasizing data wrangling, statistics, and data analysis.

This path covers the full duration of 6 months, with at least one course per period, and follows the educational principles of foundational building blocks, gradual increase in complexity, practical application, and emphasis on data storytelling and communication.

learning_path:
**Recommended Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX2668 | Basics of Digital Marketing for All | edx | Foundational understanding of digital marketing concepts, tools, and terminology. |
| 2 | EDX1344 | Fundamentals of Digital Marketing | edx | Builds on the foundational understanding by covering digital marketing strategy, inbound and outbound marketing, and mobile marketing. |
| 3 | EDX1361 | Fundamentals of Digital Marketing, Social Media, and E-Commerce | edx | Expands on the previous courses by covering social media and e-commerce techniques, and real-world application of digital marketing methods. |
| 4 | EDX3037 | Online Marketing Strategies | edx | Applies traditional marketing strategies in an online environment, helping learners evaluate a firm's internet marketing strategy. |
| 5 | EDX3449 | Social Media Marketing | edx | Focuses on creating social media content, allocating a social media advertising budget, and measuring campaign performance. |
| 6 | EDX3288 | Digital Marketing: A Strategic Perspective | edx | Takes a strategic approach to digital marketing, covering lead generation, conversions, and data-driven decision making. |

**How the path fits together**

This learning path starts with foundational courses (EDX2668 and EDX1344) that provide a solid understanding of digital marketing concepts, tools, and terminology. The next course (EDX1361) builds on this foundation by covering social media and e-commerce techniques, and real-world application of digital marketing methods. The path then shifts to online marketing strategies (EDX3037) and social media marketing (EDX3449), which focus on practical application and hands-on practice. Finally, the course on digital marketing strategy (EDX3288) takes a strategic approach, covering lead generation, conversions, and data-driven decision making. This path provides a comprehensive understanding of digital marketing and social media strategy for small business owners, with a focus on practical application and real-world examples.

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |

| 4 | EDX490 | Credit Risk Management in Banking | edx | Introduces banking-specific knowledge, including credit risk management, essential for banking careers. |
| 5 | EDX3339 | Financial Modelling and Analysis | edx | Develops analytical and critical thinking skills through financial modeling and analysis. |
| 6 | EDX1622 | Foundations of Modern Finance II | edx | Advances financial knowledge, covering valuation, portfolio optimization, and capital structure decisions. |
| 7 | EDX1304 | Portfolio Management - Theory & Practice (Part 1) | edx | Focuses on portfolio management, a critical aspect of investment analysis in banking. |
| 8 | EDX2136 | Creating Innovative Business Models | edx | Develops skills in creating innovative business models, relevant to banking and finance. |
| 9 | EDX911 | Derivatives Markets: Advanced Modeling and Strategies | edx | Explores advanced derivatives modeling and strategies, essential for investment analysis in banking. |
| 10 | EDX3389 | Real Estate Financial Analytics | edx | Introduces real estate financial analytics, a specialized area in banking and finance. |

Each course builds on the previous one, gradually increasing complexity and introducing new concepts. The path emphasizes practical application, analytical and critical thinking skills, and industry-specific knowledge, preparing learners for a career in banking.

**Learning Path for Public Health and Epidemiology Basics**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU4578 | Epidemiology in Public Health Practice Specialization | Coursera | Introduces epidemiology and its role in public health, providing a foundational understanding of the subject. |
| 2 | COU5729 | Foundations of Public Health Practice Specialization | Coursera | Builds on the foundational understanding of epidemiology by introducing public health concepts, including health protection and behavior change. |
| 3 | COU3400 | Population Health: Fundamentals of Population Health Management | Coursera | Expands on the public health concepts by focusing on population health management, including epidemiology and data analytics. |
| 4 | COU3773 | Epidemiology: The Basic Science of Public Health | Coursera | Delivers a comprehensive introduction to epidemiology, covering the distribution and determinants of diseases, health conditions, or events among populations. |
| 5 | COU3404 | Data and Health Indicators in Public Health Practice | Coursera | Develops the learner's understanding of data analysis and health indicators in public health practice, building on the epidemiology and population health management foundations. |
| 6 | COU5018 | Investigating Epidemics like COVID-19: An Analyst's Guide | Coursera | Applies epidemiological methods to real-world scenarios, such as investigating epidemics, and introduces data analysis and interpretation. |
| 7 | COU4254 | Evaluating Public Health Programs at Scale | Coursera | Focuses on program evaluation in public health, using data analysis and epidemiological methods to assess the effectiveness of programs. |

The learning path starts with an introduction to epidemiology and public health, building a foundational understanding of the subject. It then expands on these concepts, focusing on population health management, data analysis, and epidemiological methods. The path culminates in applying epidemiological methods to real-world scenarios and evaluating public health programs at scale. This progression from foundational to advanced topics, with a focus on critical thinking and analysis, will equip the learner with a comprehensive understanding of public health and epidemiology basics.

| 3 | COU6018 | Virtual Teacher Final Project | Coursera | Develops skills in instructional design and virtual education, applying knowledge in a real-world context. |

| 6 | COU6055 | Number Sense for Primary Education with PhET Simulations | Coursera | Applies theoretical knowledge to a specific subject area, developing skills in lesson planning and pedagogy. |
| 7 | COU5387 | Generative AI as a Learning Design Partner Specialization | Coursera | Introduces generative AI as a tool for learning design, enhancing teaching methods with innovative technologies. |
| 8 | COU5977 | Relationship Management | Coursera | Develops advanced skills in relationship management, communication, and conflict resolution, essential for effective teaching and leadership. |

This learning path progresses from foundational knowledge to practical application, emphasizing learner-centered approaches and innovative technologies. The sequence of courses ensures a gradual acquisition of skills, with opportunities for reflection and feedback throughout. While the available courses cover a wide range of topics, they may not fully address the learner's request for classroom teaching methods. However, the path focuses on online teaching and learning, which is a critical aspect of modern education.

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |

| 6 | EDX3096 | Content & Engagement | edX | Focuses on creating engaging content and assessing online learning, including ADA compliance and UDL. |

| 8 | EDX1929 | Instructional Design Course Evaluation & Capstone Project | edX | Focuses on evaluating and improving online courses, including learning analytics and course design. |
| 9 | COU3678 | Blended Learning: Personalizing Education for Students | Coursera | Provides advanced-level skills in blended learning, including personalized education and educational technology. |
| 10 | EDX1891 | Instructional Design and Technology: Learning Theories | edX | Focuses on learning theories and their application in instructional design, including behaviorism, cognitivism, and constructivism. |

This learning path is designed to progress from foundational to advanced skills in instructional design and building online courses. The path starts with a foundational course in virtual education and online instruction (COU6018), followed by a specialization in online learning design (COU3731). The learner then moves on to designing and developing an online course (EDX2165), focusing on practical application (EDX2784). Intermediate-level skills are introduced in creating an online course (COU1859), followed by creating engaging content and assessing online learning (EDX3096). The path then shifts to generative AI and its application in learning design (COU5387), evaluating and improving online courses (EDX1929), and finally, advanced-level skills in blended learning (COU3678) and learning theories (EDX1891). This path provides a comprehensive and practical learning experience for the learner, covering the full duration of their request.

query: Educational assessment and measuring student learning
learning_path:
**Learning Path Table**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU329 | Performance Assessment in the Virtual Classroom | Coursera | Foundational understanding of performance assessment in virtual classrooms. |
| 2 | EDX927 | Strategies for Online Teaching and Learning | edX | Building on the previous course, this one focuses on online teaching and learning strategies. |
| 3 | COU6018 | Virtual Teacher Final Project | Coursera | Practical application of online teaching and learning strategies through a final project. |
| 4 | EDX3335 | Teaching Certificate: Online and Hybrid Learning Design | edX | Advanced understanding of online and hybrid learning design, including technology integration. |
| 5 | COU3678 | Blended Learning: Personalizing Education for Students | Coursera | Applying blended learning principles to personalize education for students. |
| 6 | COU3293 | Data Science Methods for Quality Improvement Specialization | Coursera | Using data science methods to improve quality in educational settings. |
| 7 | COU4941 | Statistics with SAS | Coursera | Advanced statistical analysis using SAS, essential for data-driven decision making. |
| 8 | COU3206 | Designing, Running, and Analyzing Experiments | Coursera | Designing and analyzing experiments to inform educational decisions. |
| 9 | COU2744 | Data Literacy Capstone – Evaluating Research | Coursera | Evaluating research using data literacy skills, a key aspect of data-driven decision making. |

**Learning Path Explanation**

This learning path is designed to take the learner from foundational understanding of performance assessment in virtual classrooms to advanced data-driven decision making. The path starts with a foundational course on performance assessment in virtual classrooms (COU329), followed by a course on online teaching and learning strategies (EDX927). The learner then applies these strategies through a final project (COU6018) and advances to online and hybrid learning design (EDX3335). The path then shifts to blended learning and personalization (COU3678), followed by data science methods for quality improvement (COU3293). The learner then develops advanced statistical analysis skills using SAS (COU4941) and applies these skills to designing and analyzing experiments (COU3206). Finally, the learner evaluates research using data literacy skills (COU2744), a key aspect of data-driven decision making. This learning path covers the full duration of the learner's request and provides a comprehensive understanding of educational assessment and measuring student learning.

learning_path:
**6-Month Data Science Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Month 1 | COU4368 | Introduction to Data Science Specialization | Coursera | Foundational building block, covers data science basics |
| Month 2 | COU5253 | SQL for Data Science | Coursera | Builds on previous course, focuses on SQL skills essential for data science |
| Month 3 | COU3148 | Practical Data Science with MATLAB Specialization | Coursera | Introduces data analysis and visualization with MATLAB, a key skill for data science |
| Month 4 | COU2036 | Data Visualization with R | Coursera | Develops data visualization skills using R, a popular programming language for data science |
| Month 5 | COU3806 | Python Data Products for Predictive Analytics Specialization | Coursera | Focuses on predictive analytics and data products, a key application of data science |
| Month 6 | COU3809 | Power BI Data Analyst Prep | Coursera | Prepares learners for a data analyst role, covering data analysis, visualization, and communication |

This 6-month learning path starts with a foundational course in data science (COU4368), followed by a course that builds on this foundation by focusing on SQL skills (COU5253). The next course introduces data analysis and visualization with MATLAB (COU3148), a key skill for data science. In Month 4, learners develop data visualization skills using R (COU2036). In Month 5, they focus on predictive analytics and data products using Python (COU3806). Finally, in Month 6, they prepare for a data analyst role by covering data analysis, visualization, and communication using Power BI (COU3809).

This learning path covers the full duration requested, with at least one course per period, and progresses from foundational to advanced. The courses are chosen to provide a solid foundation in data science, build on previous knowledge, and develop key skills for data analysis, visualization, and communication.

**Machine Learning and Deep Learning Path with Python**
=====================================================

### Course Recommendations

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX2045 | Introduction to Python and Programming for Data Science and Machine Learning | edx | Foundational understanding of Python programming fundamentals |
| 2 | EDX2908 | Math for Machine Learning with Python | edx | Mathematical concepts and techniques required for machine learning |
| 3 | EDX2184 | Deep Learning Fundamentals with Keras | edx | Introduction to deep learning concepts and Keras library |
| 4 | EDX207 | Machine Learning with Python: from Linear Models to Deep Learning | edx | Supervised learning, regression, classification, and clustering |
| 5 | EDX873 | Analyzing Data with Python | edx | Data analysis, visualization, and manipulation with Pandas and NumPy |
| 6 | EDX2610 | AI for Everyone: Master the Basics | edx | Understanding AI, machine learning, and deep learning concepts |
| 7 | EDX590 | Google AI for Anyone | edx | Introduction to AI, machine learning, and deep learning with Google AI |
| 8 | EDX1856 | Data and AI Fundamentals | edx | Differentiation of AI technologies, use cases, and career opportunities |
| 9 | EDX1836 | Applied Deep Learning Capstone Project | edx | Practical application of deep learning concepts to real-world problems |
| 10 | EDX1031 | Big Data and Education | edx | Educational data mining, learning analytics, and data mining methods |

### How the Path Fits Together

This machine learning and deep learning path with Python starts with foundational courses in Python programming (EDX2045) and mathematical concepts (EDX2908). The next step is to introduce deep learning concepts and the Keras library (EDX2184). Then, the learner will explore supervised learning, regression, classification, and clustering with machine learning with Python (EDX207). Data analysis, visualization, and manipulation with Pandas and NumPy are covered in EDX873. The learner will gain a broader understanding of AI, machine learning, and deep learning concepts with EDX2610 and EDX590. Differentiation of AI technologies, use cases, and career opportunities are explored in EDX1856. Finally, the learner will apply deep learning concepts to real-world problems with EDX1836 and explore educational data mining, learning analytics, and data mining methods with EDX1031.

Note: The available courses do not fully cover the request for a comprehensive machine learning and deep learning path with Python. However, the recommended courses provide a solid foundation and a logical sequence of learning.

**Learning Path for Relearning Calculus**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX870 | College Algebra and Problem Solving | edx | Review of algebra and geometry to build a strong foundation for calculus. |
| 2 | EDX147 | MathTrackX: Integral Calculus | edx | Introduction to integral calculus, building on the algebra and geometry foundation. |
| 3 | EDX1297 | Calculus I: From Functions to Differential Equations | edx | Introduction to differential calculus, including differentiation and integration techniques. |
| 4 | EDX1281 | Maths Essentials | edx | Application of calculus to real-world problems, including optimization and modeling. |
| 5 | EDX3143 | Mathematical Techniques for Problem Solving in Engineering and Science | edx | Linear algebra and vector spaces, essential for engineering applications of calculus. |
| 6 | EDX2477 | Calculus Applied! | edx | Real-world applications of calculus, including data modeling and analysis. |
| 7 | EDX1281 | Maths Essentials | edx | Further application of calculus to real-world problems, including optimization and modeling. |
| 8 | EDX1080 | AP Calculus: Challenging Concepts from Calculus AB & Calculus BC | edx | Mastery of challenging concepts in calculus, including differential equations and optimization. |

The learning path starts with a review of algebra and geometry in EDX870, followed by an introduction to integral calculus in EDX147. EDX1297 introduces differential calculus, including differentiation and integration techniques. EDX1281 applies calculus to real-world problems, including optimization and modeling. EDX3143 covers linear algebra and vector spaces, essential for engineering applications of calculus. EDX2477 showcases real-world applications of calculus, including data modeling and analysis. The final course, EDX1080, masters challenging concepts in calculus, including differential equations and optimization.

This learning path covers the full duration requested, with at least one course per period. The courses are chosen to build on prior knowledge, gradually increase cognitive load, and emphasize problem-solving and application. The path balances depth and breadth, using real-world examples and applications to illustrate the relevance of calculus to engineering. Regular practice exercises, quizzes, and assessments will help the learner track their progress, stay motivated, and identify areas for improvement.

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX1319 | Linear Algebra - Foundations to Frontiers | edx | Foundational linear algebra concepts, including vector spaces, linear transformations, and matrix operations. |
| 2 | EDX1930 | Linear Algebra, Part 1 | edx | Building on EDX1319, this course covers the relationships between linear equations, matrices, and linear transformations. |
| 3 | EDX1522 | Computational Probability and Inference | edx | Introduces probability theory, graphical models, and algorithms for prediction and inference, which are essential for machine learning. |
| 4 | EDX2998 | Foundations of Data Science | edx | Covers the role of probability theory, optimization, and linear algebra in artificial intelligence, including probability distributions and hypothesis testing. |
| 5 | EDX2908 | Math for Machine Learning with Python | edx | Reviews mathematical concepts, including equations, functions, and graphs, and applies them to machine learning with Python. |
| 6 | EDX207 | Machine Learning with Python: from Linear Models to Deep Learning | edx | Covers machine learning principles, including classification, regression, clustering, and reinforcement learning, and applies them to real-world problems. |
| 7 | EDX1442 | Mathematical understanding of uncertainty | edx | Explores advanced probability theory, including random processes, Markov chains, and large deviation principles, which are crucial for understanding uncertainty in machine learning. |
| 8 | EDX2786 | Linear Algebra I: Vectors and Linear Equations | edx | Provides a comprehensive review of linear algebra concepts, including vector spaces, linear transformations, and matrix operations, which are essential for machine learning. |

**Learning Path for Small Business Owner in Digital Marketing and Social Media Strategy**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-2 weeks | EDX2668 | Basics of Digital Marketing for All | edx | Foundational knowledge of digital marketing tools, SEO, social media marketing, and email marketing. |
| 2-4 weeks | EDX1344 | Fundamentals of Digital Marketing | edx | Builds on foundational knowledge, covering digital marketing strategy, inbound and outbound marketing, mobile marketing, and attribution. |
| 4-6 weeks | EDX3281 | Copywriting for Digital Marketing | edx | Develops skills in creating engaging copy for digital platforms and social media, enhancing search rankings and conversions. |
| 6-8 weeks | EDX3294 | Search Engine Optimisation | edx | Applies copywriting skills to drive more traffic to the website and impact online business presence. |
| 8-12 weeks | EDX3288 | Digital Marketing: A Strategic Perspective | edx | Integrates digital marketing skills with a strategic perspective, enabling effective lead generation and conversions. |
| 12-16 weeks | EDX3449 | Social Media Marketing | edx | Develops knowledge to create social media content, allocate advertising budgets, and measure campaign performance. |
| 16-20 weeks | EDX3249 | Digital Marketing | edx | Applies strategic digital marketing skills to drive business growth, with a focus on holistic digital marketing strategy. |

This learning path starts with foundational knowledge of digital marketing tools and concepts (EDX2668), followed by a comprehensive overview of digital marketing fundamentals (EDX1344). The learner then develops skills in copywriting for digital marketing (EDX3281) and applies these skills to search engine optimization (EDX3294). The path continues with a strategic perspective on digital marketing (EDX3288), social media marketing (EDX3449), and finally, a holistic digital marketing strategy (EDX3249). Each course builds on the previous one, gradually increasing complexity and depth, and emphasizing practical application and real-world examples.

| 1 | COU3088 | An Introduction to American Law | Coursera | This course provides a foundational understanding of American law, covering common law and the constitution. It's a beginner-level course that sets the stage for further exploration of law. |
| 2 | COU380 | A Law Student's Toolkit | Coursera | Building on the foundational understanding of American law, this course introduces learners to legal terminology, concepts, and tools used by lawyers and legal academics. It's essential for developing a solid foundation in legal reasoning. |
| 3 | COU3527 | European Business Law Specialization | Coursera | This course applies the foundational understanding of law to a specific context, European business law. It helps learners understand how law is used in a real-world setting, making the learning experience more engaging and relevant. |
| 4 | COU6043 | Introduction to Environmental Law and Policy | Coursera | This course introduces learners to environmental law, a critical area of law that intersects with human liberty and economic aspirations. It builds on the foundational understanding of law and applies it to a complex, real-world issue. |
| 5 | COU1139 | AI & Law | Coursera | This course explores the intersection of law and technology, specifically artificial intelligence. It requires learners to apply their understanding of law to a rapidly evolving field, promoting critical thinking and analysis. |

### How the path fits together

This learning path introduces non-lawyers to law and legal reasoning through a gradual and contextual approach. It starts with a foundational understanding of American law (COU3088), then builds on that understanding with a law student's toolkit (COU380). The path then applies this knowledge to a specific context, European business law (COU3527), and a complex, real-world issue, environmental law (COU6043). Finally, it introduces learners to the intersection of law and technology, AI & Law (COU1139). This path provides a comprehensive introduction to law and legal reasoning, covering foundational concepts, real-world applications, and critical thinking and analysis.

**Learning Path Table**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU923 | Getting Started With Music Theory | Coursera | Foundational knowledge of music theory, including pitch, rhythm, and notation. |
| 2 | COU4357 | Developing Your Musicianship Specialization | Coursera | Building on the foundational knowledge, this course introduces chord progressions, scales, and music theory in a practical context. |
| 3 | COU2512 | Approaching Music Theory: Melodic Forms and Simple Harmony | Coursera | Expanding on music theory concepts, this course covers melodic forms and simple harmony, preparing the learner for more advanced composition. |
| 4 | COU2108 | Developing Your Musicianship: Final Project | Coursera | Applying music theory concepts through composition, this course helps the learner develop their musicianship skills and create a final project. |
| 5 | COU455 | FL Studio Basics | Coursera | Introducing music production software, this course enables the learner to apply music theory concepts in a practical context and start composing. |
| 6 | COU5891 | Music Production: Crafting Award-Worthy Songs Specialization | Coursera | Building on music production skills, this course covers songwriting, vocal production, and music recording, helping the learner refine their composition skills. |
| 7 | COU5618 | The Art of Music Production | Coursera | Advanced music production techniques, including audio production and music recording, help the learner refine their composition skills and produce high-quality music. |

**Learning Path Explanation**

This learning path starts with foundational music theory knowledge, building incrementally to more advanced composition and music production skills. The learner begins with "Getting Started With Music Theory" (COU923) to establish a solid understanding of music theory concepts. Next, "Developing Your Musicianship Specialization" (COU4357) introduces chord progressions, scales, and music theory in a practical context. "Approaching Music Theory: Melodic Forms and Simple Harmony" (COU2512) expands on music theory concepts, preparing the learner for more advanced composition. "Developing Your Musicianship: Final Project" (COU2108) applies music theory concepts through composition, helping the learner develop their musicianship skills. "FL Studio Basics" (COU455) introduces music production software, enabling the learner to apply music theory concepts in a practical context and start composing. Finally, "Music Production: Crafting Award-Worthy Songs Specialization" (COU5891) and "The Art of Music Production" (COU5618) help the learner refine their composition skills and produce high-quality music. This learning path balances theoretical and practical learning, encourages experimentation and exploration, and fosters a growth mindset and motivation.

This path covers the full duration of the learner's request, with at least one course per period, and provides a logical and sequential progression of topics.
